+//! Diagnostics to the launching terminal (#163): one `tracing`
+//! subscriber for every binary, printing to stderr, filtered by
+//! `CAMCRAFT_LOG` (else `RUST_LOG`, else [`DEFAULT_FILTER`]). The seams
+//! that emit - project save/load, post writes, generation, command
+//! dispatch - carry their own `tracing` events; this module only
+//! decides where they go.
+//!
+//! Provenance: the `tracing` / `tracing-subscriber` crates' documented
+//! fmt + EnvFilter setup. Our own wiring, no vendor material.
+
+use std::path::Path;
+use std::time::Instant;
+
+use tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter;
+
+/// Milliseconds since `started`, saturating at `u64::MAX` rather than
+/// truncating the `u128` `as_millis` returns (safe numeric conversion).
+#[must_use]
+pub fn elapsed_ms(started: Instant) -> u64 {
+    u64::try_from(started.elapsed().as_millis()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)
+}
+
+/// The file name a log line shows for `path`: the name only, never the
+/// folder, so a log pasted into a bug report does not expose the user's
+/// directory layout. A path with no final name shows as given.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn file_name(path: &Path) -> String {
+    path.file_name()
+        .map_or_else(|| path.display().to_string(), |n| n.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
+}
+
+/// Quiet by default: the app's own info lines, the GPU stack's warnings.
+/// `CAMCRAFT_LOG=debug` (or `RUST_LOG=camcraft_app=debug`) opens it up.
+pub const DEFAULT_FILTER: &str = "info,wgpu_core=warn,wgpu_hal=warn,naga=warn,winit=warn";
+
+/// The filter the environment asks for, falling back to the default.
+/// Invalid directives are ignored by name in the filter itself, never a
+/// panic (Prime Directive).
+#[must_use]
+pub fn filter_from_env() -> EnvFilter {
+    EnvFilter::try_from_env("CAMCRAFT_LOG")
+        .or_else(|_| EnvFilter::try_from_default_env())
+        .unwrap_or_else(|_| EnvFilter::new(DEFAULT_FILTER))
+}
+
+/// Install the stderr subscriber. Safe to call more than once (a test
+/// harness, a second entry point): only the first install wins, later
+/// calls are no-ops.
+pub fn init() {
+    let _ = tracing_subscriber::fmt()
+        .with_env_filter(filter_from_env())
+        .with_writer(std::io::stderr)
+        .with_target(true)
+        .try_init();
+}

+## #163 - terminal logging through `tracing` (2026-11-07, first slice)
+
+- **Chosen:** `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` (fmt + env-filter, stderr),
+  installed once by `camcraft_app::logging::init()` from both binaries
+  (`camcraft`, `camcraft-cli`). Filter from `CAMCRAFT_LOG`, else
+  `RUST_LOG`, else `info` with the GPU stack (`wgpu_core`, `wgpu_hal`,
+  `naga`, `winit`) at `warn`; `tracing-log` bridges their `log` records.
+- **Seams instrumented:** project save/open (path, bytes, or why not),
+  NC post (path, bytes, ops, lines, ms - or "NC program not written:
+  <why>"), every generation (op name span, kind, moves, warnings, ms, or
+  the refusal at warn; the job carries the op name so batch runs log it
+  too), command dispatch (`execute command=<Type>` at debug, undo too).
+- **Not in this slice:** converting the ~185 `println!`/`eprintln!`, and
+  per-limit "which budget fired" events inside generators (their refusal
+  text already rides the warn line) - follow-up work on #163.
+- **Dropped:** `log` + `env_logger` (no spans, so batch generations
+  could not carry their op name); a log file (the issue asks for the
+  launching terminal).
+- **Review fixes (PR #222, 2026-11-08):** log lines name the file only
+  (`file=part.camproj`), never its folder, so a log pasted into a bug
+  report does not expose the user's directory layout
+  (`logging::file_name`); durations go through `logging::elapsed_ms`,
+  which saturates at `u64::MAX` instead of an `as` cast. Dropped: keeping
+  absolute paths with a docs note (the terminal is local, but logs get
+  pasted).
